newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs rally late to close mostly up on covering.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs rally late to close mostly up on covering.

text.p: CME hog futures rallied late on pre-weekend short covering to end mostly higher with August again setting a new contract high, traders noted. Pork bellies ended lower but above the day's lows.

Hog futures closed 0.250 cent per lb lower to 0.525 higher with February off most at 78.450 cents. August paced the gain and finished at 73.600 cents after setting a new contract high for the third consecutive day.
"(The rally) appears to just be evening up ahead of the weekend," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.
Summer months again were bolstered by last week's bullish Hogs and Pigs report.

Levitt cited gains in live cattle and a rebound during the day in pork belly futures before values again dipped in that pit, as supportive to hog futures. But the strength may fade as cash markets may again be pressured next week, he added.

Much weaker-than-expected pork prices should keep packer bids for cash hogs weak next week, traders said. Pork cutout values have fallen over $4 per cwt in the past two weeks and expectations are for cash hogs to trade another $0.50 per cwt lower on Monday, they said.

Cargill Investor Services turned a buyer in February late after selling early and buying by Rand Financials offset early mixed selling in April. Buy stops added to gains. Rand and ABN Chicogo Corp bought June early, pit sources said.
In hog options, volatility in February was easing with First Chicago offering 78 calls early. LIT division of First Options sold February 78 calls late, pit sources added.
Pork belly futures rose for net gains around midday on local short covering before slipping late. However, renewed local covering pared losses again in the closing range, traders said.
Expectations of increased pork sales later in the month and continued strength in cash bellies also provided support, they said.
"January is usually a good bacon (usage) month," one trader said.
Prudential Securities bought early and R.J. O'Brien sold late into the local short covering, pit sources said of activity in the pork belly pit.
Pork bellies closed 0.125 to 0.600 cent per lb lower with February off the least at 81.375 cents.
